section_summary: This section contains diplomatic summaries and translations of monitored Japanese broadcasts about wartime production, trade, transport, food, taxation, labor, and administration in Japan and occupied territories. It also includes a Board of Economic Warfare appraisal that identifies shipping and industrial processing capacity as major limits on Japan’s use of acquired raw materials. Covering despatches from Chungking transmit fuller translations of broadcasts previously summarized by telegram.

subfiles.title: Economic reports from Japanese and European broadcasts
subfiles.about: Continues a numbered digest of industrial, agricultural, transport, and financial developments in Japan and Europe.
subfiles.summary: The surviving portion reports Japanese controls over textiles, metals, shipbuilding, timber, oil, tobacco, and food production, alongside developments in the Philippines, Hong Kong, and Shanghai. A European section covers Romanian infrastructure and mineral exports, German materials savings and coal output, French artificial fibers, and Spanish railway equipment.

subfiles.title: Japanese economic broadcasts, section one
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Japanese trade group, textile equipment transfers to the Philippines, and proposed tax increases.
subfiles.summary: A new trade group will control material stocks and exports. Japan plans deeper spinning and weaving restrictions, shipment of surplus equipment to the Philippines, and increased fiscal revenue from taxes.

subfiles.title: Japanese economic broadcasts, section two
subfiles.about: Reports food, shipping, prisoner labor, banking, rice cultivation, and Philippine–Shanghai trade.
subfiles.summary: Broadcasts claim Hainan rice self-sufficiency, revised wooden-vessel plans, use of prisoners in Philippine cotton harvesting, a German bank in Tokyo, Formosan rice trials in Penang, and renewed Philippine–Shanghai barter.

subfiles.title: Monitored Japanese economic broadcasts
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Summarizes Chinese monitoring of Japanese reports on prices, industry, labor, transport, taxes, and occupied-area resources.
subfiles.summary: The digest reports a Shanghai wholesale-price freeze, state supervision of Japanese iron factories, prisoner labor, coal mining, and restored Java railways. It also gives Nanking revenue estimates and Japanese claims about minerals, sugar, cotton, oil, and rice in Southeast Asia.

subfiles.title: Monitored Japanese economic broadcasts, section one
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Reports transport restoration, resource exports, cotton supply, and North China mining.
subfiles.summary: Reports proposed Canton–Taiwan navigation, Malayan exports and rice gains, difficulty obtaining Chinese cotton, restored Malayan and Sumatran transport, and increased North China coal production.

subfiles.title: Monitored Japanese economic broadcasts, section two
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Continues the resource and transport digest with oil, Hong Kong industry, food crops, textiles, and investment.
subfiles.summary: Reports restored or partially restored oil and mineral facilities in Borneo and nearby islands, Hong Kong shipbuilding and factories, proposed sweet-potato cultivation, possible transfer of Japanese spinning to China, and North China Development Company investments.

subfiles.title: Monitored Japanese broadcasts, March 3–10
subfiles.about: Summarizes food goals, regional shortages, forestry, air service, and Yangtze trade restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Reports Shanghai rations, Japanese food-production targets, surplus sugar and coconut oil hampered by transport shortages, Manchurian tree planting, resumed Hanoi–Saigon flights, and eased lower Yangtze commodity controls.

subfiles.title: Monitored Japanese economic broadcasts
subfiles.about: Summarizes Shanghai commodity restrictions and reported development in Manchuria, Sumatra, Burma, and the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Reports controls on goods entering and leaving Shanghai, production drives and hydroelectric works in Manchuria, rubber and railway development in Sumatra, Burmese food and textile plans, and restored Philippine communications.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on bi-monthly appraisal
subfiles.about: Flags the appraisal’s discussion of Japan’s processing capacity.
subfiles.summary: Notes that processing capacity trails Japan’s acquisition of raw materials.

subfiles.title: Bi-monthly appraisal of Japan’s economic position
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s wartime raw materials, food, transport, processing capacity, labor, and economic administration.
subfiles.summary: The appraisal finds that Japan is improving access to raw materials, especially in nearby continental territories, while shipping losses and inadequate processing capacity limit their use. It examines iron, coal, metals, cotton, food supply, small wooden ships, rail transport, and new industrial areas. It also describes labor mobilization in Japan and occupied territories and the growing power of Tojo and the army-dominated Planning Board over priority industries.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 960 transmitting broadcast translations
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits fuller translations behind earlier broadcast summaries.

subfiles.title: Economic items from broadcasts, December 10, 1942–January 3, 1943
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Translates selected Japanese and Nanking broadcasts on budgets, transport, production, finance, and controls.
subfiles.summary: Items cover Japan’s 1943 budget; communications in Malaya and Sumatra; road, railway, ship, and junk construction; petroleum controls; Philippine coconut production; and North China food, irrigation, and cotton projects. Later entries address Manchukuo and North China budgets, enemy-property rules, banknote issuance, bank mergers, and scrap collection.

subfiles.title: Economic items from broadcasts, January 4–18, 1943
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Translates selected broadcasts on trade, banking, taxes, resources, food, and transport.
subfiles.summary: Items describe the closing of Yokohama silk markets, planned Japan–Indochina trade arrangements, communications in North Borneo, rubber controls, a South China economic meeting, and power generation on the Yalu River. They also cover Manchukuo spending, banking and currency in occupied China and Malaya, Japanese tax increases, mineral surveys, Java cotton, and Mongolian trade.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 970 transmitting broadcast translations
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits translations supporting February 17 and 25 telegram summaries.
subfiles.summary: Encloses fuller translations of January 19–February 3 broadcasts.

subfiles.title: Economic items from broadcasts, January 19–23, 1943
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Details the Japanese trade group and developments in textiles, taxation, shipping, labor, banking, and barter.
subfiles.summary: Translations elaborate the new trade group law, movement of surplus spinning equipment to the Philippines, higher Japanese taxes, Hainan agriculture, and standardized wooden vessels. They also report use of American and Filipino prisoners for cotton harvesting, a German bank in Tokyo, Formosan rice trials in Penang, and Philippine–Shanghai trade.

subfiles.title: Economic items from broadcasts, January 23–February 3, 1943
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Details price and industrial controls, prisoner and civilian labor, transport repairs, taxation, and South Seas resources.
subfiles.summary: Items expand on Shanghai’s wholesale-price freeze, state control of Japanese iron factories, prisoner labor, Guangdong coal mining, silk consolidation, and the movement of Chinese workers. They also report Manchurian coal output, Java railway repairs, Nanking tax estimates, and Japanese claims about oil, minerals, food, and shipping across Southeast Asia.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 988 transmitting broadcast translations
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, U.S. Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Transmits fuller translations supporting the March 4 telegram.

subfiles.title: Economic items from broadcasts, February 3–28, 1943
subfiles.to: Department of State; Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Begins the enclosure with reports on Canton–Taiwan shipping, Malayan recovery, and cotton supply.
subfiles.summary: The opening items discuss proposed wooden-vessel trade between Canton and Taiwan, Malayan exports and food production, and Japanese plans to expand cotton cultivation in China and the Philippines. A review of Malaya and Sumatra begins on page 195 and continues beyond this section.
